subject: science
prompt:
# How Big Can One Cell Get?

A cell that is good at surviving grows. And then it keeps growing.

> **Is there a size at which growing stops being an advantage?**

Take a position before the lesson argues one.

options.text: No - a bigger cell is always a better cell.
options.feedback: Worth committing to, because the lesson is about to show you exactly where this breaks.

options.text: Yes - past a point the inside of the cell is more than its surface can supply and one set of instructions can run.
Yes, but only because large cells are easier for predators to find.
options.feedback: Being spotted is a real cost, but the limit turns up even with nothing hunting the cell.

options.text: No, as long as the cell keeps adding more organelles.
options.feedback: More departments help. Hold this thought and see whether it is enough.
